extracted.intended_audience: manufacturers of commercial packaged boilers, industry stakeholders, regulatory compliance officers, and legal practitioners interacting with DOE energy-efficiency standards
extracted.subtask_description: Final rule amending energy conservation standards for commercial packaged boilers (CPB): definitions, applicability, effective dates, and required efficiency levels by equipment category/subcategory and certified rated input. Includes background on court remand/vacatur and procedural justification for immediate final rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'commercial packaged boiler' (CPB)
rubrics_metrics.description: A commercial packaged boiler is a packaged boiler that meets all of the following requirements: (1) has rated input of 300,000 Btu/h or greater; (2) is to any significant extent, distributed in commerce for space conditioning and/or service water heating in buildings but does not meet the definition of 'hot water supply boiler'; (3) does not meet the definition of 'field-constructed'; and (4) is designed to operate a steam pressure at or below 15 psig; operate at or below a water pressure of 160 psig and water temperature of 250 °F, or operate at a steam pressure at or below 15 psig and at or below a water pressure of 160 psig and water temperature of 250 °F.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cites 10 CFR 431.82 as the regulatory source for the CPB definition. Use this multi-part definition to determine whether a particular boiler model falls within the scope of the CPB standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability — meet indicated energy conservation standard on/after effective date (general rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each commercial packaged boiler listed in table 1 of this paragraph (a) and manufactured on or after the effective date listed must meet the indicated energy conservation standard.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies to items listed in the accompanying tables; compliance obligation attaches to manufacture date on or after the table's effective date. See paragraph (a) and paragraph (b) for table-specific instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Table 1 applicability and effective date (March 2, 2012) — general
rubrics_metrics.description: Each commercial packaged boiler listed in table 1 of paragraph (a) and manufactured on or after the effective date listed must meet the indicated energy conservation standard (Table 1 effective date: March 2, 2012).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Table 1 entries specify equipment category, subcategory, certified rated input ranges, and efficiency levels (notation uses E_C and E_T where defined). Manufacturers must ensure models manufactured on or after March 2, 2012 meet the stated efficiencies in Table 1.

rubrics_metrics.name: Table 1 — Hot Water Commercial Packaged Boilers; Gas-fired; ≥300,000 Btu/h and ≤2,500,000 Btu/h
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpreted per the table: thermal efficiency (E_T) of 80.0% required for gas-fired hot water CPBs rated between 300,000 and 2,500,000 Btu/h manufactured on/after March 2, 2012.

rubrics_metrics.name: Table 1 — Hot Water Commercial Packaged Boilers; Gas-fired; >2,500,000 Btu/h
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For gas-fired hot water CPBs with certified rated input above 2,500,000 Btu/h, a combustion efficiency (E_C) of 82.0% is specified for models manufactured on/after March 2, 2012.

rubrics_metrics.name: Table 1 — Hot Water Commercial Packaged Boilers; Oil-fired; ≥300,000 Btu/h and ≤2,500,000 Btu/h
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Oil-fired hot water CPBs rated between 300,000 and 2,500,000 Btu/h must meet a thermal efficiency (E_T) of 82.0% for units manufactured on/after March 2, 2012.

rubrics_metrics.name: Table 1 — Hot Water Commercial Packaged Boilers; Oil-fired; >2,500,000 Btu/h
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Oil-fired hot water CPBs with certified rated input above 2,500,000 Btu/h must meet a combustion efficiency (E_C) of 84.0% for models manufactured on/after March 2, 2012.

rubrics_metrics.name: Table 1 — Steam Commercial Packaged Boilers; Gas-fired, all, except natural draft; ≥300,000 Btu/h and ≤2,500,000 Btu/h
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gas-fired (non-natural-draft) steam CPBs in this input range must meet thermal efficiency (E_T) of 79.0% for units manufactured on/after March 2, 2012.

rubrics_metrics.name: Table 1 — Steam Commercial Packaged Boilers; Gas-fired, all, except natural draft; >2,500,000 Btu/h
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Same 79.0% E_T requirement applies for >2,500,000 Btu/h for gas-fired (except natural draft) steam CPBs manufactured on/after March 2, 2012.

rubrics_metrics.name: Table 1 — Steam Commercial Packaged Boilers; Gas-fired—natural draft; ≥300,000 Btu/h and ≤2,500,000 Btu/h
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Natural-draft gas-fired steam CPBs in this input range must meet thermal efficiency (E_T) of 77.0% for models manufactured on/after March 2, 2012.

rubrics_metrics.name: Table 1 — Steam Commercial Packaged Boilers; Gas-fired—natural draft; >2,500,000 Btu/h
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Same 77.0% E_T requirement applies for >2,500,000 Btu/h natural-draft gas-fired steam CPBs manufactured on/after March 2, 2012.

rubrics_metrics.name: Table 1 — Steam Commercial Packaged Boilers; Oil-fired; ≥300,000 Btu/h and ≤2,500,000 Btu/h
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Oil-fired steam CPBs in this input range must meet thermal efficiency (E_T) of 81.0% for units manufactured on/after March 2, 2012.

rubrics_metrics.name: Table 1 — Steam Commercial Packaged Boilers; Oil-fired; >2,500,000 Btu/h
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Same 81.0% E_T requirement applies for >2,500,000 Btu/h oil-fired steam CPBs manufactured on/after March 2, 2012.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpretation note — E_C and E_T definitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Where E_C is combustion efficiency and E_T is thermal efficiency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these definitions to interpret the efficiency values in Table 1 and Table 2 (i.e., whether the stated percentage refers to combustion efficiency or thermal efficiency).

rubrics_metrics.name: Table 2 applicability and effective date (March 2, 2022) — general
rubrics_metrics.description: Each commercial packaged boiler listed in table 2 of paragraph (b) and manufactured on or after the effective date listed in Table 2 must meet the indicated energy conservation standard (Table 2 effective date: March 2, 2022).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Table 2 entries specify updated efficiency obligations with a later effective date (March 2, 2022); manufacturers must comply for models manufactured on or after that date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Table 2 — Steam Commercial Packaged Boilers; Gas-fired—natural draft; ≥300,000 Btu/h and ≤2,500,000 Btu/h
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For natural-draft gas-fired steam CPBs in this input range, thermal efficiency (E_T) of 79.0% is required for units manufactured on/after March 2, 2022.

rubrics_metrics.name: Table 2 — Steam Commercial Packaged Boilers; Gas-fired—natural draft; >2,500,000 Btu/h
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Same 79.0% E_T requirement applies for >2,500,000 Btu/h natural-draft gas-fired steam CPBs manufactured on/after March 2, 2022.

rubrics_metrics.name: DOE action — vacatur of January 2020 Final Rule and amendment of standards
rubrics_metrics.description: This final rule is amending DOE's standards for commercial packaged boilers in compliance with a U.S. Court of Appeals D.C. Circuit decision vacating the January 10, 2020 rule that amended standards for CPB.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Background: the D.C. Circuit found DOE failed to provide meaningful responses to comments on three modeling issues (random assignment of boiler efficiencies to buildings; forecasted fuel prices; estimated burner operating hours), remanded the rule to DOE to cure those failures, and later vacated the energy conservation standards established in January 2020. DOE is implementing the court's order by vacating the current standards via this final rule; compliance and rulemaking history affect the legal status of standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedural justification — waiver of prior notice and comment (good cause)
rubrics_metrics.description: This final rule is not subject to the requirement to provide prior notice and an opportunity for public comment pursuant to 5 U.S.C. 553(b)(B). DOE finds good cause to waive the requirement to provide prior notice and an opportunity for public comment as such procedure is unnecessary because DOE must comply with the order of a Federal court and has no discretion to do otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DOE states that providing notice/comments would serve no useful purpose given the court-ordered nature of the action; this explains why the agency issued an effective final rule without routine notice-and-comment procedures.
